cues.subtitle: A Depository contract is deployed on a local test chain (an EVM). It will hold each bank's reserves and the collateral of every bilateral account, and it enforces disputes.
cues.title: The Depository is deployed
cues.tradfiParallel: The settlement system the banks hold accounts in, run as a contract instead of an operator ledger.
cues.what: A Depository contract is deployed on a local test chain (an EVM). It will hold each bank's reserves and the collateral of every bilateral account, and it enforces disputes.
cues.why: The Depository is the only shared ledger here. Payments happen in bilateral accounts; the chain is used for funding, collateral and enforcement.

cues.subtitle: Alice, Hub and Bob register on the Depository. Each bank is controlled by its own signing key.
cues.title: Three banks register
cues.tradfiParallel: Opening accounts in the settlement system before doing business.
cues.what: Alice, Hub and Bob register on the Depository. Each bank is controlled by its own signing key.
cues.why: Registration gives each bank an identity whose signatures the contract can verify.

cues.subtitle: Hub's reserve on the Depository is credited with 10,000,000 USDC of a USDC test token.
cues.title: Test balances credited on the Depository
cues.tradfiParallel: Settled in the Depository's settlement asset (here a USDC test token; in a central bank deployment, tokenised reserves).
cues.what: Hub's reserve on the Depository is credited with 10,000,000 USDC of a USDC test token.
cues.why: A reserve is a balance held on the Depository itself. It funds collateral and on-chain transfers.

cues.subtitle: Hub queues two on-chain transfers in one batch: 3,000,000 USDC to Alice and 2,000,000 USDC to Bob.
cues.title: Hub sends Alice and Bob their test balances
cues.tradfiParallel: Two gross transfers in one submission.
cues.what: Hub queues two on-chain transfers in one batch: 3,000,000 USDC to Alice and 2,000,000 USDC to Bob.
cues.why: In this demo the test balances come from Hub. In a deployment each bank deposits its own funds; no hub injects capital.

cues.subtitle: The batch waits for the next block on the test chain.
cues.title: Waiting for the next block
cues.tradfiParallel: An instruction submitted to the settlement system but not yet settled.
cues.what: The batch waits for the next block on the test chain.
cues.why: Until the block is final nothing has moved, so the account cannot count the collateral yet.

cues.subtitle: The block is final: Alice holds 3,000,000 USDC and Bob 2,000,000 USDC of reserves. Hub keeps 5,000,000 USDC.
cues.title: Transfers executed on-chain
cues.tradfiParallel: Settled in the Depository's settlement asset (here a USDC test token; in a central bank deployment, tokenised reserves).
cues.what: The block is final: Alice holds 3,000,000 USDC and Bob 2,000,000 USDC of reserves. Hub keeps 5,000,000 USDC.
cues.why: These reserves now belong to Alice and Bob, not to Hub.

cues.subtitle: Alice transfers 500,000 USDC from her reserve to Bob's on the Depository.
cues.title: Alice pays Bob directly on-chain
cues.tradfiParallel: A gross transfer between two settlement accounts, as in an RTGS.
cues.what: Alice transfers 500,000 USDC from her reserve to Bob's on the Depository.
cues.why: Any two participants can transfer reserves on-chain: gross, and final when the block is final. The bilateral accounts that follow avoid doing this for every payment.

cues.subtitle: Hub 5,000,000 · Alice 2,500,000 · Bob 2,500,000 USDC. The total is unchanged at 10,000,000 USDC.
cues.title: Reserves in place
cues.tradfiParallel: Settled in the Depository's settlement asset (here a USDC test token; in a central bank deployment, tokenised reserves).
cues.what: Hub 5,000,000 · Alice 2,500,000 · Bob 2,500,000 USDC. The total is unchanged at 10,000,000 USDC.
cues.why: Everything so far was on-chain. Next, two bilateral accounts take payments off-chain.

cues.subtitle: Alice and Hub open a bilateral account. Both keep an identical copy of its state, and every change is a frame both of them sign.
cues.title: Alice opens an account with Hub
cues.tradfiParallel: A correspondent relationship backed by one jointly signed record instead of two ledgers to reconcile.
cues.what: Alice and Hub open a bilateral account. Both keep an identical copy of its state, and every change is a frame both of them sign.
cues.why: The account involves only the two banks that carry its risk; nothing about it is registered network-wide.

cues.subtitle: Bob opens his own account with Hub. Alice and Bob have no account with each other; Hub connects them.
cues.title: Bob opens an account with Hub
cues.tradfiParallel: Two respondent banks using the same correspondent.
cues.what: Bob opens his own account with Hub. Alice and Bob have no account with each other; Hub connects them.
cues.why: Each bank's exposure stays inside its own account with Hub.

cues.subtitle: Alice instructs the Depository to move 500,000 USDC from her reserve into collateral for her account with Hub. The instruction goes on-chain in a batch.
cues.title: Alice posts 500,000 USDC of collateral
cues.tradfiParallel: Collateral locked per counterparty plays the nostro's role, but in a neutral contract.
cues.what: Alice instructs the Depository to move 500,000 USDC from her reserve into collateral for her account with Hub. The instruction goes on-chain in a batch.
cues.why: Collateral lets Alice pay Hub without Hub having to trust her: whatever she owes Hub in the account is covered on the Depository.

cues.subtitle: The batch waits for the next block on the test chain.
cues.title: Waiting for the next block
cues.tradfiParallel: An instruction submitted to the settlement system but not yet settled.
cues.what: The batch waits for the next block on the test chain.
cues.why: Until the block is final nothing has moved, so the account cannot count the collateral yet.

cues.subtitle: The block is final. Alice's reserve falls from 2,500,000 USDC to 2,000,000 USDC and her account with Hub holds 500,000 USDC of collateral. Both banks sign the account frame that records it.
cues.title: Collateral recorded on the Depository
cues.tradfiParallel: Pledged collateral, held by the contract rather than by Hub.
cues.what: The block is final. Alice's reserve falls from 2,500,000 USDC to 2,000,000 USDC and her account with Hub holds 500,000 USDC of collateral. Both banks sign the account frame that records it.
cues.why: Alice can now pay Hub up to 500,000 USDC off-chain, fully covered by collateral.

keyMetrics: Hub may owe Bob: up to 500,000 USDC
cues.subtitle: Bob sets a 500,000 USDC limit on what Hub may owe him in their account. Nothing is deposited; Bob and Hub both sign the new limit.
cues.title: Bob gives Hub a 500,000 USDC credit line
cues.tradfiParallel: A bilateral credit limit on a correspondent, set by the bank that carries the risk.
cues.what: Bob sets a 500,000 USDC limit on what Hub may owe him in their account. Nothing is deposited; Bob and Hub both sign the new limit.
cues.why: Only the receiving bank sets this limit, and it can lower it at any time: a lower limit blocks new exposure but never erases debt already incurred. The most Hub can ever owe Bob unsecured is Bob's own limit. Intraday credit here comes from the receiving bank, not from the central bank.

cues.subtitle: On a local test chain, Alice, Hub and Bob hold test balances on the Depository. Alice's account with Hub holds 500,000 USDC of her collateral; Bob has given Hub a 500,000 USDC credit line.
cues.title: Starting point: the same three banks as Part 1
cues.tradfiParallel: The same correspondent set-up as Part 1.
cues.what: On a local test chain, Alice, Hub and Bob hold test balances on the Depository. Alice's account with Hub holds 500,000 USDC of her collateral; Bob has given Hub a 500,000 USDC credit line.
cues.why: This part changes one thing: every payment is conditional on a secret, so it either completes on every hop or on none of them.

cues.subtitle: Alice pays Bob 125,000 USDC as a hash-locked payment. She locks 125,000.125 USDC in her account with Hub (the payment plus Hub's fee). Hub can claim it only with a secret that only Bob can decrypt from the payment's routing data.
cues.title: Payment 1 of 2: Alice locks 125,000.125 USDC to Hub
cues.tradfiParallel: A chain of conditional payments tied to one secret: either every hop completes, from payee back to payer, or every lock expires and is refunded. Intermediaries carry the timing risk.
cues.what: Alice pays Bob 125,000 USDC as a hash-locked payment. She locks 125,000.125 USDC in her account with Hub (the payment plus Hub's fee). Hub can claim it only with a secret that only Bob can decrypt from the payment's routing data.
cues.why: Every hop is locked to the same hash. Either the secret travels back and every hop completes, or the locks expire and are refunded.

cues.subtitle: Hub co-signs Alice's lock and offers Bob a matching lock under the same hash, with an earlier expiry.
cues.title: Hub locks the payment onward to Bob
cues.tradfiParallel: A correspondent passing a conditional payment on against matching cover.
cues.what: Hub co-signs Alice's lock and offers Bob a matching lock under the same hash, with an earlier expiry.
cues.why: Hub's outgoing lock is matched by the incoming lock it holds. Its risk is timing: it must claim Alice's lock with the secret before that lock expires.

cues.subtitle: Bob decrypted the secret and used it to claim his lock; Hub then used the same secret to claim Alice's. 125,000 USDC moved from Alice to Bob, and Hub kept a 0.125 USDC fee.
cues.title: Payment 1 complete: the secret travelled back
cues.tradfiParallel: Irrevocable between the two banks once both sign, and enforceable on-chain up to the account's collateral; above that it is an unsecured claim. Settlement in the asset happens when collateral covers it or it moves on-chain; legal finality depends on system designation.
cues.what: Bob decrypted the secret and used it to claim his lock; Hub then used the same secret to claim Alice's. 125,000 USDC moved from Alice to Bob, and Hub kept a 0.125 USDC fee.
cues.why: Revealing the secret completes each hop in turn, from payee back to payer.

badges.detail: Signed by both banks of each account: neither can undo it alone.
badges.label: Bilateral

badges.detail: Enforceable at the Depository up to collateral: Alice's lock in full; Bob's 125,000 USDC is an unsecured claim on Hub.
badges.label: On-chain

badges.detail: Depends on whether the system is designated under settlement-finality law.
badges.label: Legal

cues.subtitle: Irrevocable between the two banks once both sign, and enforceable on-chain up to the account's collateral; above that it is an unsecured claim. Settlement in the asset happens when collateral covers it or it moves on-chain; legal finality depends on system designation.
cues.title: How final is payment 1?
cues.tradfiParallel: Conditionality is not settlement: Bob still holds an unsecured claim on Hub for what collateral does not cover.
cues.what: Irrevocable between the two banks once both sign, and enforceable on-chain up to the account's collateral; above that it is an unsecured claim. Settlement in the asset happens when collateral covers it or it moves on-chain; legal finality depends on system designation.
cues.why: The hash lock decides whether the payment happens; it does not make Hub's debt to Bob any more secured than in Part 1.

cues.subtitle: Alice pays Bob another 125,000 USDC the same way: one lock per hop, one secret.
cues.title: Payment 2 of 2: another 125,000 USDC
cues.tradfiParallel: A chain of conditional payments tied to one secret: either every hop completes, from payee back to payer, or every lock expires and is refunded. Intermediaries carry the timing risk.
cues.what: Alice pays Bob another 125,000 USDC the same way: one lock per hop, one secret.
cues.why: Each conditional payment costs a few signatures per account, not an on-chain transaction.

cues.subtitle: Alice's collateral covers everything she has paid Hub. Hub now owes Bob 250,000 USDC with nothing posted against it.
cues.title: Payments complete: 250,000 USDC from Alice to Bob
cues.tradfiParallel: An unsecured interbank exposure inside an agreed limit.
cues.what: Alice's collateral covers everything she has paid Hub. Hub now owes Bob 250,000 USDC with nothing posted against it.
cues.why: Bob carries 250,000 USDC of unsecured exposure to Hub, within the 500,000 USDC limit he set. Rebalancing will collateralise it.

cues.subtitle: Bob pays Alice 50,000 USDC through Hub, hash-locked the same way, over the same two accounts.
cues.title: Bob pays Alice 50,000 USDC back
cues.tradfiParallel: Bilateral netting by construction.
cues.what: Bob pays Alice 50,000 USDC through Hub, hash-locked the same way, over the same two accounts.
cues.why: Each account keeps one net position, so payments in opposite directions offset inside it.

cues.subtitle: 300,000 USDC of payments leave one net position per account: Alice has paid Hub 200,000.25 USDC net, inside her collateral, and Hub owes Bob 199,999.95 USDC net.
cues.title: Net positions after three payments
cues.tradfiParallel: Continuous bilateral netting, pair by pair.
cues.what: 300,000 USDC of payments leave one net position per account: Alice has paid Hub 200,000.25 USDC net, inside her collateral, and Hub owes Bob 199,999.95 USDC net.
cues.why: Only net positions would ever need settling. There is no multilateral netting across accounts, and collateral stays locked per counterparty.

cues.subtitle: Bob records, in his own runtime, that he wants at least 100,000 USDC of collateral in his account with Hub and will pay up to 10 USDC for a top-up. The policy stays private to Bob.
cues.title: Bob records a collateral policy
cues.tradfiParallel: An internal collateral threshold, comparable to one agreed in a credit support annex.
cues.what: Bob records, in his own runtime, that he wants at least 100,000 USDC of collateral in his account with Hub and will pay up to 10 USDC for a top-up. The policy stays private to Bob.
cues.why: The bank carrying the exposure decides how much of it must be collateralised.

cues.subtitle: Hub moves 200,000 USDC from its own reserve into collateral for its account with Bob, in an on-chain batch. In this demo Hub does it directly; the request path from Bob's policy is not exercised here.
cues.title: Hub posts 200,000 USDC of collateral
cues.tradfiParallel: Posting collateral from a bank's own settlement account.
cues.what: Hub moves 200,000 USDC from its own reserve into collateral for its account with Bob, in an on-chain batch. In this demo Hub does it directly; the request path from Bob's policy is not exercised here.
cues.why: Moving its own reserve into collateral needs only Hub's signature: it can only improve Bob's position.

cues.subtitle: The batch waits for the next block on the test chain.
cues.title: Waiting for the next block
cues.tradfiParallel: An instruction submitted to the settlement system but not yet settled.
cues.what: The batch waits for the next block on the test chain.
cues.why: Until the block is final nothing has moved, so the account cannot count the collateral yet.

cues.subtitle: The block is final: the Hub–Bob account holds 200,000 USDC of collateral against Hub's debt to Bob.
cues.title: Bob's claim on Hub is collateralised
cues.tradfiParallel: Collateral posted once an exposure passes the agreed threshold.
cues.what: The block is final: the Hub–Bob account holds 200,000 USDC of collateral against Hub's debt to Bob.
cues.why: Credit lines stay open, so new payments can create unsecured exposure again until the next top-up.

cues.subtitle: A new bank, Charlie, opens an account with Hub, and both sides grant each other 50,000 USDC of credit. Charlie holds no reserve on the Depository.
cues.title: Charlie joins through Hub
cues.tradfiParallel: A respondent bank opening a correspondent account on credit terms.
cues.what: A new bank, Charlie, opens an account with Hub, and both sides grant each other 50,000 USDC of credit. Charlie holds no reserve on the Depository.
cues.why: Joining the network is one bilateral account. Nothing changes for Alice or Bob.

cues.subtitle: Hub 2 opens accounts with Hub and with Bob, with 100,000 USDC credit lines each way, creating a longer route from Alice to Bob.
cues.title: A second hub joins
cues.tradfiParallel: A chain of correspondent banks.
cues.what: Hub 2 opens accounts with Hub and with Bob, with 100,000 USDC credit lines each way, creating a longer route from Alice to Bob.
cues.why: A payment can cross several intermediaries. Each hop is a separate bilateral account with its own limits.

cues.subtitle: Alice pays Bob 25,000 USDC over three hops: Alice → Hub → Hub 2 → Bob. Every hop is locked to the same hash; the secret, which only Bob can decrypt, releases them one by one, from Bob back to Alice.
cues.title: A three-hop hash-locked payment
cues.tradfiParallel: A chain of conditional payments tied to one secret: either every hop completes, from payee back to payer, or every lock expires and is refunded. Intermediaries carry the timing risk.
cues.what: Alice pays Bob 25,000 USDC over three hops: Alice → Hub → Hub 2 → Bob. Every hop is locked to the same hash; the secret, which only Bob can decrypt, releases them one by one, from Bob back to Alice.
cues.why: Each intermediary decrypts only its own layer of the route: the next hop and the amount to forward, not who paid or who is paid. The same hash appears on every hop, so intermediaries that collude can link them.

cues.subtitle: The secret travelled back over all three hops. Bob received 25,000 USDC; Hub and Hub 2 each kept a routing fee, and no lock is left open.
cues.title: Three-hop payment complete
cues.tradfiParallel: A chain of conditional payments tied to one secret: either every hop completes, from payee back to payer, or every lock expires and is refunded. Intermediaries carry the timing risk.
cues.what: The secret travelled back over all three hops. Bob received 25,000 USDC; Hub and Hub 2 each kept a routing fee, and no lock is left open.
cues.why: No hop completed before the one after it: an intermediary claims its incoming lock only with the secret that has already paid its outgoing one.

cues.subtitle: Alice sends Hub 1 USDC while Hub is unreachable for one step. The message waits; when Hub reconnects, both sign the update.
cues.title: Hub drops offline for a moment
cues.tradfiParallel: Store-and-forward messaging: an instruction waits for the counterparty instead of being dropped.
cues.what: Alice sends Hub 1 USDC while Hub is unreachable for one step. The message waits; when Hub reconnects, both sign the update.
cues.why: Inputs queue while a party is offline, and both sides converge on the same signed state when it returns.
